mechanism: Both drugs possess anticholinergic and CNS depressant properties; disulfiram may inhibit metabolism of meclizine through CYP450 enzyme inhibition, potentially increasing meclizine levels and adverse effects.
action: Monitor for increased anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, urinary retention, confusion) and CNS depression; consider alternative antiemetic if excessive sedation or anticholinergic toxicity occurs.
